```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(PGViS)
set.seed(1)
```

## What the score is measuring

A germline variant that lands inside a splice donor site or a transcription
factor binding site may or may not break it. PGViS asks a model trained on
that class of element to score the reference sequence and the mutated
sequence, and treats a large drop in confidence as evidence of disruption.

That alone does not distinguish a variant that is disruptive from one that is
disruptive *and* enriched in your cohort. So PGViS also compares the cohort
allele frequency against a matched population frequency; that shift is used to
*select* variants and is deliberately kept out of the score itself. The score
ranks each variant's regulatory change and log-odds ratio within its cohort's
variant list and summarises the variants a person carries as one number per
sample.

Three components:

```{r metrics-demo}
# strongly disruptive: model is confident before, not after
log_odds_ratio(p_ref = 0.97, p_alt = 0.03)
score_change(0.97, 0.03)

# a variant enriched in the cohort relative to the population
d <- data.frame(af_ref = 0.60, af_alt = 0.40,
                pop_af_ref = 0.95, pop_af_alt = 0.05)
pgvis_delta_wi(d, transform = FALSE, keep_raw = TRUE)[, c("delta_af_alt", "delta_wi")]
```

`score_change` deliberately shrinks toward zero when the model is unconfident
either way:

```{r shrinkage}
c(confident = score_change(0.9, 0.7), unconfident = score_change(0.3, 0.1))
```

Both pairs differ by 0.2 in probability, but only the first is a change the
model actually stands behind.

## Setting up a project

Everything site-specific lives in one object.

```{r config}
cfg <- pgvis_config(
  root       = file.path(tempdir(), "demo"),
  cohorts    = c("luad", "lusc"),
  thresholds = list(ref_prob_min = 0.7, alt_prob_max = 0.3)
)
cfg
```

Note that the thresholds you did not specify keep their defaults rather than
disappearing — the strict `0.7 / 0.3` pair above still inherits the 5% carrier
floor and the 10 bp indel limit.

```{r stages}
pgvis_stages()[, c("stage", "description")]
```

Each shell stage is rendered with your configuration prepended, and either
written for inspection or submitted:

```{r render, eval = FALSE}
pgvis_call_gvcf(cfg, sample_sheet = "samples.tsv", submit = FALSE)
#> [PGViS] Rendered 02_call_gvcf.sh -> .../logs/02_call_gvcf.run.sh
```

## Coordinate keys

Joins between the variant table and the prediction table are the place where
this kind of pipeline usually goes wrong, because the two sides get built by
different scripts with different key formats. PGViS has one constructor each,
and they round-trip:

```{r keys}
k <- func_site_key("chr7", 55019000, 55019080, "-")
v <- variant_key("chr7", 55019032, 55019033, "a", "g")
c(k, v)
parse_key(v, "variant")
```

Strandless features (TFBS) get an empty `()` so keys stay comparable across
feature types:

```{r keys-strandless}
func_site_key("chr7", 100, 400, ".", stranded = FALSE)
```

## Building the sequences

Given a region and a variant inside it, PGViS extracts the region on the
feature strand, applies the variant in that frame, and emits both sequences as
k-mers. The substitution is deliberately forgiving about coordinates — the
reference allele is searched for in a small window, because region BEDs and
variant BEDs are produced by different tools and can disagree by a base — but
it will not invent a result:

```{r mutate}
mutate_sequence("A", "G", "TTTATTT", pos_start = 4, pos_end = 4)  # exact
mutate_sequence("A", "G", "TTTATTT", pos_start = 5, pos_end = 5)  # off by one
mutate_sequence("CCCC", "G", "TTTATTT", pos_start = 4, pos_end = 7)  # wrong allele
```

The last returns `NA` rather than a plausible-looking wrong sequence. Those
rows are counted and reported, and are worth investigating rather than
dropping silently.

```{r kmer}
seq2kmer("ACGTACGTAC", k = 6)
```

## Population frequency resolution

UCSC's dbSNP track packs per-project frequencies into one comma-delimited
string. PGViS walks the projects in priority order and takes the first whose
reported minor allele matches one of the variant's alleles.

```{r popaf}
row <- data.frame(
  dbsnp_freqs = paste(c("0.11", "", "0.13", rep("", 9), "0.19"), collapse = ","),
  dbsnp_minor = paste(c("A",    "", "A",    rep("", 9), "A"),    collapse = ","),
  dbsnp_ref = "G", dbsnp_alt = "A"
)
pgvis_resolve_population_af(row)[, c("pop_af_alt", "pop_af_ref", "freq_source")]
```

Priority is an argument, not a hard-coded cascade:

```{r popaf-priority}
pgvis_resolve_population_af(row, priority = c("1000G", "TOPMED"))$freq_source
```

When nothing matches, the result is `NA` and `freq_source == "none"` — not a
guess.

## Scoring

```{r score}
The score has four steps. For a dataset with variant list $U$ and a sample
carrying the variants $C_i$:

$$p_{fv} = \frac{\#\{u \in U : x_{fu} \le x_{fv}\}}{|U|}, \quad f \in \{|\Delta Wi|, \mathrm{LOR}\} \tag{1}$$
$$s_v = \left(p_{|\Delta Wi|,v}\, p_{\mathrm{LOR},v}\right)^{1/2} \tag{2}$$
$$S_i = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{|C_i|}\textstyle\sum_{v \in C_i} s_v^{2}} \tag{3}$$
$$\mathrm{PGViS}_i = (S_i - \mathrm{mean}_{\mathrm{ref}}) / \mathrm{SD}_{\mathrm{ref}} \tag{4}$$

ΔAF is not used: it is the criterion that selects the variants, so scoring on
it again would be circular.

```{r score}
set.seed(1)
mk <- function(cohort, n, n_list, pre, enrich) {
  vars <- data.frame(var_site = paste0(pre, seq_len(n_list)),
                     delta_wi_int = rnorm(n_list), log_odds_ratio = rnorm(n_list))
  prob <- if (enrich) rank(abs(vars$delta_wi_int) * rank(vars$log_odds_ratio))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    v <- vars[sample(n_list, sample(5:30, 1), prob = prob), ]
    v$sample <- paste0(substr(cohort, 1, 1), i); v$cohort <- cohort
    v$superpopulation <- if (i %% 2) "EUR" else "EAS"; v
  }))
}
long <- rbind(mk("1000Genomes", 100, 80, "r", FALSE),
              mk("tumour",      100, 200, "t", TRUE))

long       <- pgvis_variant_score(long)    # Eq. 1-2
per_sample <- pgvis_sample_scores(long)    # Eq. 3
scored     <- pgvis_score(per_sample, reference_group = "1000Genomes")   # Eq. 4
head(scored[, c("sample", "cohort", "superpopulation", "pgvis_raw", "pgvis")])
attr(scored, "reference")
```

Here the tumour samples preferentially carry the high-ranking variants of
their own list, which is what the score detects. The reference cohort sits at
zero by construction (within each superpopulation); the test cohort is
displaced:

```{r score-check}
tapply(scored$pgvis, scored$cohort, median)
```

### Two things to get right

**Freeze the reference when you move to a validation cohort.** By default the
reference mean and SD are refit from the reference samples in front of you, so
two runs are not on the same scale unless you say so:

```{r frozen, eval = FALSE}
ref <- attr(discovery_scores, "reference")
val <- pgvis_score(validation, reference = ref)
```

The pre-0.2.0 PCA-weighted composite is still available as
`pgvis_score(df, method = "pca")`.

**Do not turn off ancestry stratification casually.** Allele-frequency
divergence from a reference panel is confounded with genetic distance from
that panel. `strata = NULL` is available for a genuinely homogeneous cohort
and is the wrong choice otherwise.

## Comparing groups

```{r compare}
d <- data.frame(pgvis = c(rnorm(120, 0), rnorm(120, 1.1)),
                group = rep(c("control", "case"), each = 120))
pgvis_compare_groups(d, min_n = 50, n_perm = 500)[, c("n1", "n2", "auc", "cohens_d", "perm_p")]
```

Below `min_n` per group, statistics are withheld rather than reported with a
caveat — an effect size from a dozen samples is not something to put on a
figure.

```{r compare-small}
small <- data.frame(pgvis = rnorm(20), group = rep(c("a", "b"), 10))
pgvis_compare_groups(small, min_n = 50)$label
```
